scenarios.title: Read+Update discovery carries operations and no Transactional member

requirements.selectedText: `operations` is required in Read+Update and Transactional and prohibited in Read. The history, receipt, snapshot, changefeed, and Event members are required only in Transactional and prohibited in both lower profiles.

scenarios.title: Read+Update discovery limits carry no Transactional capability group

requirements.selectedText: the Read+Update discovery document's `limits` is `readUpdateAdvertisedLimits`, a closed definition of its own that shares every limit primitive with `advertisedLimits`, restates the `page`, `request`, `resource`, `selector`, `patch`, and `sequence` groups unchanged, carries the `validation` group, and rejects the `transaction` group and the Transactional `retention.receipt` and `retention.replay` members
the Read discovery document's `limits` is `advertisedLimits`, which admits no `validation` group
A group is relevant only when the advertised profile exposes that capability.

scenarios.title: The Operation Directory lists exactly the six singleton targets plus sequence

requirements.selectedText: A Read+Update Scope's directory contains exactly the six singleton targets plus `sequence`:

scenarios.title: Read+Update offers no alias mutation target

requirements.selectedText: Alias creation, repointing, and deletion are mutation surface deferred beyond the Read+Update profile: its Operation Directory is exactly the six singleton targets plus `sequence`, so a Read+Update Scope serves alias resolution over aliases established administratively

scenarios.title: create-bead returns the created postimage with an allocated or honored id

requirements.selectedText: If `id` is omitted, the authority allocates one.
`created` and `updated` carry `resource`, the complete Resource record as a `GET` of its URL would now return it

scenarios.title: update-bead-properties applies the patch and retains the revision on a semantic no-op

requirements.selectedText: Applying the patch must yield a JSON object satisfying every effective Type schema.
A semantic no-op update, defined under [Revisions](#revisions), succeeds with outcome `updated` and the retained revision.

scenarios.title: delete-bead returns the deleted identity and refuses a Bead with live incident Links

requirements.selectedText: `deleted` carries `deleted`, the absolute canonical URL of the removed Resource, and no record: deletion mints no version.
After a Bead or Link is deleted, ordinary `GET`, `view=properties`, and, for a Bead, `view=links` return the same `404` `resource-not-found` problem used for an unknown or non-visible identity.
`incident-links-exist`: a Bead deletion reached while a live Link is incident upon the Bead.

scenarios.title: A deletion blocked by hidden incident Links withholds them

requirements.selectedText: `incident-links-exist`: a Bead deletion reached while a live Link is incident upon the Bead. A non-disclosing authority withholds the hidden Links that caused it.

scenarios.title: create-link canonicalizes endpoint spellings and echoes a pin byte-identically

requirements.selectedText: A durable relative endpoint reference resolves against the canonical Scope URL, not against the request URL or the containing Link URL, and must name a live Bead.
The pin is provenance, not a constraint: an authority stores and echoes it byte-identically, compares it only for equality, and performs no semantic validation, dereferencing, or interpretation

scenarios.title: update-link-properties returns the Link postimage; an unowned Link's update versions no endpoint

requirements.selectedText: `created` and `updated` carry `resource`, the complete Resource record as a `GET` of its URL would now return it
An owned Link remains a first-class Link with its own URL and its own revision: a caller addresses, reads, and updates it there like any other Link.
Creating or deleting a Link does not mutate an in-Scope endpoint Bead or change that Bead's Resource revision

scenarios.title: delete-link returns the deleted identity and the Link then reads as 404

requirements.selectedText: `deleted` carries `deleted`, the absolute canonical URL of the removed Resource, and no record: deletion mints no version.
After a Bead or Link is deleted, ordinary `GET`, `view=properties`, and, for a Bead, `view=links` return the same `404` `resource-not-found` problem used for an unknown or non-visible identity.

scenarios.title: Effectful owned-Link mutations carry source and sourceRevision and version the source; unowned ones carry neither and version no endpoint

requirements.selectedText: Every mutation of an owned Link versions the source Bead.
the result additionally carries `source`, the source Bead's absolute canonical URL, and `sourceRevision`, the source Bead's resulting revision, on creation, update, and deletion alike
`source` and `sourceRevision` are absent from every other result, and each is present exactly when the other is.
Creating or deleting a Link does not mutate an in-Scope endpoint Bead or change that Bead's Resource revision

scenarios.title: An owned-Link semantic no-op retains the Link's revision and attribution and reports the source's unchanged revision

requirements.selectedText: On a semantic no-op update `sourceRevision` is the source's unchanged current revision.
then the operation retains the existing revision and emits no `updated` Event
a write whose `properties` are a no-op mints no revision and records no attribution.

scenarios.title: The attribution input is recorded on every minted version; a no-op keeps the prior version's revision and attribution

requirements.selectedText: An operation that mints more than one version records its one attribution on every version it mints
a write whose `properties` are a no-op mints no revision and records no attribution.
The member is absent when no attribution was recorded.

scenarios.title: A matching expectedRevision applies and a stale one fails with revision-mismatch

requirements.selectedText: `expectedRevision` remains optional for updates and deletes, and it produces a conflict on mismatch.
`revision-mismatch`: the member's `expectedRevision` is not the Resource's current revision.

scenarios.title: Concurrent guarded updates: exactly one applies, the other fails with revision-mismatch

requirements.selectedText: The authority applies the operation only if the Resource still has that revision.
At commit, the authority also ensures that concurrent transactions cannot jointly violate those invariants.

scenarios.title: A hidden subject fails with the uniform resource-not-found

requirements.selectedText: A member's subject Resource or in-Scope endpoint Bead that does not exist or is not visible in the request's Authorization View fails with the Read profile's `resource-not-found`, under the same non-disclosure rule

scenarios.title: A missing, malformed, or repeated Idempotency-Key is rejected before execution

requirements.selectedText: A key outside the profile is rejected before execution with `malformed-request`, as is a singleton request that omits the field or carries it more than once: the authority rejects a repeated `Idempotency-Key` field rather than choosing an occurrence.

scenarios.title: An unauthenticated mutation request is rejected before admission and creates no disposition

requirements.selectedText: A request rejected before admission — an unauthenticated principal, a carrier-level rejection — creates no disposition.
| `unauthenticated` | `authentication` | 401 | `after-state-change` |

scenarios.title: A singleton retry under the same key returns the retained disposition without re-execution

requirements.selectedText: the key is retained with the same semantic identity: the authority does not execute the member and returns the retained disposition
A retained `created` result therefore always carries the same authority-allocated identity
a singleton whose key is retained, in flight, conflicting, or expired answers exactly as the corresponding sequence member would, as a direct response.

scenarios.title: The same key with different semantics fails with idempotency-conflict

requirements.selectedText: the key is retained with a different semantic identity: the member fails with `idempotency-conflict`, nothing executes, and the retained disposition is unchanged;

scenarios.title: A non-JSON or undeclared request body media type is rejected with unsupported-media-type; parameters are ignored

requirements.selectedText: `unsupported-media-type`: a mutation-target request whose body media type is not `application/json` or is not declared; media-type parameters such as `charset` are ignored.

scenarios.title: Mutation targets answer other methods with a bodyless 405 and Allow: POST, and honor the CORS OPTIONS exception

requirements.selectedText: A mutation target responds `405 Method Not Allowed` with `Allow: POST` to every other method, and the Operation Directory responds `405` with `Allow: GET, HEAD` to every method but those two
when cross-origin access is enabled, `OPTIONS` is answered according to the CORS rules rather than with `405` and joins `Allow`; listing it in `Allow` is not the preflight behavior

scenarios.title: A singleton request spelling @name, bare or pinned, is rejected before execution

requirements.selectedText: A singleton never accepts `@name`, bare or within a Pinned Reference; the bundle's singleton request definitions reject the spelling, so it is carrier syntax rejected before execution with `malformed-request`.

scenarios.title: A singleton success carries no ETag and no Location

requirements.selectedText: carries no `ETag` and no `Location`: the operation target is not the Resource's URL, and the result's `resource.id` and `resource.revision` say what those fields would.

scenarios.title: Members run strictly in order and a failure leaves earlier successes committed

requirements.selectedText: starts members strictly in declaration order and never runs them in parallel;
commits each successful member immediately and never rolls it back because a later member fails;
continues after a failed member so later independent work can run;

scenarios.title: A binding is usable after its creating member commits; a failed creator fails only its dependent

requirements.selectedText: The binding becomes available only after the create commits
A reference to a creating member whose retained disposition is a failure fails that member with `binding-unavailable`, a retained failure

scenarios.title: A dependent of a transient creator fails transiently, claims nothing, and does not stop later independent members

requirements.selectedText: the member fails with `idempotency-in-progress`, the authority consults no key state for it, executes nothing, retains nothing, and releases its claim on the member's key
A member whose `@name` reference names a creating member of the same request whose disposition was transient is transient by the same rule
Neither prevents later independent members from running.

scenarios.title: An expired creator still binds its dependent through the tombstone's allocated identity and kind

requirements.selectedText: and, for a creation that allocated an identity, that identity and its Resource kind, through which a later `@name` reference still resolves
or an `idempotency-expired` disposition, whose tombstone keeps the identity the creation allocated and its Resource kind
resolves each `@name` reference to the identity its creating member bound — taken from that member's fresh, retained, or expired disposition, never from the spelling

scenarios.title: Retained failures answer a retry unchanged, exactly as retained successes do

requirements.selectedText: Every other disposition, success or failure, is retained, and a retained failure answers a retry exactly as a retained success does for as long as it is retained
A retained disposition is returned without re-executing anything.
Re-keying a creating member changes the identity of every member that references its binding: a client that corrects a creator presents new keys for its dependents as well.

scenarios.title: A member problem carries its would-be status, operationIndex, and operationName inside 200 OK

requirements.selectedText: Each failed member contains the same Problem Details shape with its would-be `status`, its zero-based `operationIndex`, and, when the member declared one, its `operationName`.
Every entry carries `operationIndex`, the member's zero-based position in the request's `operations` array, and carries `operationName` exactly when the member declared `name`.

scenarios.title: A member-level after-delay problem may carry retryAfter; nothing else does

requirements.selectedText: A member problem whose `retry` is `after-delay` MAY carry `retryAfter`, a non-negative integer of delay-seconds: the member-level counterpart of `Retry-After`, which has no carrier inside a `200 OK` envelope.

scenarios.title: Carrier syntax failures, static @name errors included, are rejected before execution and nothing executes

requirements.selectedText: `operations` is bounded by `sequence.operations` when that limit is advertised; a longer sequence is rejected before execution with `limit-exceeded`.

Two members of one sequence MUST NOT carry the same `idempotencyKey`; a sequence that repeats a key is rejected before execution with `malformed-request`, as is one whose `name` values repeat or whose key or name violates its syntax.

A `@name` reference that is forward, unknown, or of the wrong Resource kind is carrier syntax, decidable from the request text: the sequence is rejected before execution with `malformed-request`, exactly as a batch rejects it.
a sequence request that carries the field is rejected before execution with `malformed-request`.
are direct problem responses and execute nothing

scenarios.title: Schema validity is not admission: the contextual checks the bundle cannot express are enforced by the authority

requirements.selectedText: The bundle validates wire shape, not admission.

Scope containment of durable references, Resource kind, `@name` resolution and its kind, ownership — whether `source` and `sourceRevision` apply to a Link result — correspondence between a result and its request
so does a durable reference whose spelling is not a canonical reference of the required kind or that names a Resource of another kind — the subject does not exist as the required kind

scenarios.title: A retried sequence returns every retained disposition at the present member's position

requirements.selectedText: the key is retained with the same semantic identity: the authority does not execute the member and returns the retained disposition, positioned with the present member's `operationIndex` and `operationName`;
The authority runs the remaining members to their terminal dispositions and retains those dispositions under their keys, so a retry recovers a lost response member by member.

scenarios.title: An admitted sequence runs to completion after client disconnection and a retry recovers the lost response

requirements.selectedText: Once the authority has admitted a sequence — validated its carrier and operation-record syntax and started its first member — client disconnection does not decide any member's outcome.
The authority runs the remaining members to their terminal dispositions and retains those dispositions under their keys, so a retry recovers a lost response member by member.

scenarios.title: An internal fault mid-sequence is the body-less 500; durable dispositions stay retained and the faulting claim is cleared

requirements.selectedText: an unexpected internal fault is the body-less `500` under [Problem details](#problem-details) even mid-sequence. Members that reached a durable disposition before it stay retained, the faulting member's claim is cleared
An implementation MUST respond to an unexpected internal server fault with a body-less `500 Internal Server Error`

scenarios.title: No sequence-wide lock: an unrelated request completes between members and the later member observes its commit

requirements.selectedText: permits unrelated requests to interleave between members, taking no sequence-wide transaction, reservation, or lock.
Because unrelated mutations may interleave, a bound Resource may change or be deleted before a later member uses it.

scenarios.title: A concurrent duplicate fails with idempotency-in-progress, and a delayed retry receives the retained disposition once one exists

requirements.selectedText: the key is in flight — claimed by a request whose member has not reached a terminal outcome: the member fails with `idempotency-in-progress`, the authority executes nothing and retains nothing for the presenting member, and a retry after the delay receives the retained disposition once the first presentation has reached a retained outcome
a delayed retry may instead find the key still in flight, meet a transient disposition of its own, or, after a long delay, find the disposition expired

scenarios.title: Keys are claimed at admission, so a concurrent resubmission cannot run ahead of the original

requirements.selectedText: A sequence claims every member's unknown key at admission, in declaration order, before its first member starts; a singleton claims its key before executing.
so it can neither execute a member ahead of the original's earlier members nor retain a disposition the original would contradict

scenarios.title: A concurrent retry never poisons the first presentation's dependent member

requirements.selectedText: so that a retry after the delay executes the creator and then the dependent, and a concurrent retry can never poison the dependent member of the request that first presented the keys

scenarios.title: A transient disposition is never retained and a later presentation executes

requirements.selectedText: A disposition whose `retry` is `after-delay` — `rate-limited`, `temporarily-unavailable`, and `idempotency-in-progress` — is transient and is never retained: the member was not executed, and a later member presenting the same key executes it.

scenarios.title: Semantic identity ignores labels, defaults, member order, and spelling, and includes pins, attribution, guards, and array order

requirements.selectedText: expands protocol defaults such as an omitted `properties`, preserves the order of `change` and every other array, ignores JSON object member order, and excludes `idempotencyKey` and `name`
Opaque external URIs and Pinned References are compared byte-exactly as written; `expectedRevision` and `attribution` are members of the record and therefore of its identity.

scenarios.title: Keys are scoped to the authenticated principal, not to carried attribution

requirements.selectedText: the pair of the canonical Scope URL and the authenticated principal, an anonymous principal counting as one principal
it is not the carried `attribution.principal`, which is data under [Carried attribution](#carried-attribution) and takes no part in the namespace

scenarios.title: Sequence and singleton carriers share one key namespace and one semantic identity

requirements.selectedText: The namespace is shared by every mutation carrier in the profile: a sequence member and a singleton request that present the same key in the same namespace present the same key.
Singleton and sequence forms share one idempotency namespace, one semantic-identity rule, and one retention rule.

scenarios.title: A replay after an Authorization View change is re-authorized and never executes or replaces the retained disposition

requirements.selectedText: Authorization View changes do not create a new namespace: the principal-bound disposition remains retained and cannot execute again

before returning a retained `created` or `updated` result the authority re-authorizes disclosure of the retained record — the record as retained, whether or not the Resource still exists — against the present view

When the view no longer projects that record, the member fails with `forbidden` and discloses nothing retained. That response is not retained: it replaces neither the disposition nor its semantic identity, it permits no execution

scenarios.title: A retained forbidden survives a grant for the interval; the principal presents a new key

requirements.selectedText: Every other disposition, success or failure, is retained, and a retained failure answers a retry exactly as a retained success does for as long as it is retained
Authorization View changes do not create a new namespace: the principal-bound disposition remains retained and cannot execute again

scenarios.title: An advertised retention.idempotency is honored; without one no client-known recovery window exists

requirements.selectedText: An authority retains each retained disposition for at least `retention.idempotency` after the member's terminal outcome when it advertises that limit
When it is not, no client-known recovery window exists

scenarios.title: A discarded disposition answers idempotency-expired and never re-executes; different semantics remain a conflict

requirements.selectedText: Presenting an expired key with the same semantic identity fails with `idempotency-expired`; the authority never executes the member again and never reports the discarded outcome.
Presenting an expired key with a different semantic identity remains `idempotency-conflict`.

scenarios.title: A forgotten failure leaves its key unknown; committed dispositions keep their tombstones

requirements.selectedText: A retained failure committed nothing: after the interval the authority MAY forget it entirely, and a later presentation of its key is unknown and executes
For a disposition that committed state — `created`, `updated` including a semantic no-op, or `deleted` — it MUST then retain a compact tombstone

scenarios.title: Mutation and disposition are one durable unit; restart and failover recover retries without a second mutation

requirements.selectedText: an authority MUST NOT commit a mutation without retaining its disposition under its key, and MUST NOT retain a disposition for a mutation it did not commit
A claim abandoned by a crash — one whose member reached no durable disposition — is cleared during restart or failover, so a retry executes the member once
Every mutation route — each singleton target, the sequence target, and every replica that accepts mutations — consults one authoritative key state for the namespace

scenarios.title: After an authority crash mid-sequence, recovery resumes nothing and a resubmission completes the sequence

requirements.selectedText: When the authority fails mid-sequence, members that reached a durable disposition stay retained, the member in flight is recovered as an abandoned claim, and unstarted members are never executed by recovery: the authority does not resume a sequence.
The client resubmits the sequence; retained dispositions answer the committed members, and the remaining members execute in order.

scenarios.title: A restore that loses recovery state is a different logical Scope at a different canonical Scope URL

requirements.selectedText: A restore that cannot preserve it creates a different logical Scope under [Scopes and identity](#scopes-and-identity), at a different canonical Scope URL
A restore that cannot preserve that guarantee creates a different logical Scope and therefore uses a different canonical Scope URL.

Read+Update exposes no epoch: a client cannot detect a restore except through a changed canonical Scope URL, and the profile offers no restore signal beyond `resource-not-found`, `revision-mismatch`, and `idempotency-expired`.

scenarios.title: Every Read+Update code serializes with its exact family, status, retry, media type, and cache policy

requirements.selectedText: The Read+Update profile inherits the complete Read table unchanged and adds the rows below.
Each code fixes its HTTP status and retry disposition.
Scope-bounded representations that depend on authorization use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

scenarios.title: An inadmissible result fails with validation-failed and an uninstalled Type with type-not-installed

requirements.selectedText: `validation-failed`: the mutation is well-formed but its result is not admissible
A mutation that names an unavailable Type fails as `type-not-installed`; the mutation does not initiate installation.

scenarios.title: Type-contract failures carry diagnostics naming the effective Type and keyword location within advertised bounds

requirements.selectedText: When the failure is an effective Type contract, every entry names the failing effective Type in `type` and the failed keyword in `schemaLocation`
an authority that omits entries beyond a bound MUST advertise that bound, keeps at least one entry in evaluation order, and sets `diagnosticsTruncated` to `true`
A Resource validation failure returns a bounded diagnostic list identifying the failing effective Type and schema location

scenarios.title: A supplied id that was ever committed, including a deleted one, fails with identity-taken

requirements.selectedText: If `id` is supplied, its canonical Resource URL must never previously have been committed for any Resource in the logical Scope. Deletion does not make it available again.
`identity-taken`: a supplied `id` whose canonical Resource URL was ever committed in the logical Scope, including a deleted one.
This is inherently an existence signal for the identity the creator chose, hidden or deleted alike

scenarios.title: A mutation that would cross a maximum endpoint multiplicity fails with aggregate-constraint-violation

requirements.selectedText: Authorities MUST produce serializable outcomes when concurrent mutations could cross a maximum.
`aggregate-constraint-violation`: the mutation would violate a Scope aggregate policy — in BDP v0, a maximum endpoint multiplicity.

scenarios.title: An oversized request body is rejected with request-too-large before execution

requirements.selectedText: `request.bodyBytes` counts octets in the representation body
| `request-too-large` | `size` | 413 | `never` |

scenarios.title: Every mutation response carries Cache-Control: private, no-store

requirements.selectedText: Mutation responses carry `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

scenarios.title: Enabled CORS allows Idempotency-Key and exposes Retry-After

requirements.selectedText: its CORS policy MUST allow every BDP-defined non-safelisted request field used by its advertised profile, including `Idempotency-Key`
It MUST expose `Link`, `ETag`, `Retry-After`, `Cache-Control`
